mentions.name: Liquid Labor
mentions.description: An economic framework that departs from traditional labor economics by treating machine hours as 'liquid labor' with perfect elasticity. It replaces headcount-based GDP measurement with a National Autonomous Work Index (NAWI) and models robotics as the conversion of energy into a labor reserve deployable with perfect elasticity, either as policy or as a Robots as a Service (RaaS) business model. The framework argues nations that build reserves of autonomous hours will survive a Great Stagnation, while those relying on shrinking human labor pools face a terminal liquidity crisis and greater centralization.
mentions.problem: Traditional GDP measurement via human headcount overlooks machine labor; amid shrinking world population, record budget deficits, and hyper-financialization, nations relying on shrinking human labor pools face a terminal liquidity crisis during a Great Stagnation.
mentions.source_excerpt: I’ve been diving into a Liquid Labor framework (liquid-labor.com), it’s a departure from traditional labor economics. It moves us away from measuring GDP via human headcounts and toward a National Autonomous Work Index (NAWI) treating machine hours as liquid labor with perfect elasticity of labor.
